notes:
Hermes ships a NATIVE autonomous self-prompting loop: /goal <text> registers a standing goal, immediately enqueues the goal text as the first user message, and after every turn a judge call decides done/continue — on continue the '[Continuing toward your standing goal]' prompt is fed back into the SAME session as an ordinary user message (hermes_cli/goals.py, cli.py:_maybe_continue_goal_after_turn). Each iteration is therefore a complete turn that ends with finish_reason='stop' BEFORE the judge is consulted, so the store legitimately reports turn-over between iterations and the daemon cycles ready/working per iteration rather than holding one continuous working span — the same relaxation the claudecode sibling documented for its Stop-hook /goal. What this spec asserts instead is the thing that actually proves autonomy: iter2_start must reach working with NO driver-sent message between iter1_done and it. hermes is a PRESESSION adapter here — ProcessOwnedStore whose sessions row is INSERTed only on the first user message, so a transient proc-<PID> row is born first and the real store session (a different id) is born ready afterwards; every post-birth phase anchors to the real session. observations: tokens verified nonzero on live sessions rows (input_tokens ~16k); cost_nonzero=false is provisional (hermes reports estimated_cost_usd=0.0 subscription-included and irrlicht re-prices from its alias table, which has no gpt-5.6-luna entry); model left UNPINNED for record to fill because the recording home's config.yaml is not knowable from here.

RECORD-TIME FINDINGS (2026-08-03, recording 2-7 on daemon 7731c37, coexist daemon on :7838): 7/7 phases green on the first take.
(1) THE AUTONOMY PROOF IS IN THE TRANSCRIPT, not merely in the state arc. Iterations 2 and 3 each begin with a `user` row the driver never typed - literally "[Continuing toward your standing goal]\nGoal: ..." - written by the CLI's goal loop after the previous turn's finish_reason='stop'. The driver's only inputs were the single `/goal ...` line at the start and `/goal clear` at the end; everything between iter1_done and loop_terminated is the agent re-prompting itself. Recorded arc, all on the ONE store-backed session 20260803_005638_2b9159: ready(00:56:43.82) -> working(.86) -> ready(00:56:49.81) -> working(00:56:51.82) -> ready(00:56:57.80) -> working(00:57:01.82) -> ready(00:57:09.82). Three iterations, three finish_reason='stop' assistant rows saying 1, 2, 3.
(2) The arc is PER-ITERATION ready<->working, not one continuous working span, and that is the correct rendering for hermes: each iteration is a complete turn whose closing assistant row carries finish_reason='stop', so watcher.turnIsDone marks it Terminal and the session settles ready before the continuation prompt re-opens it ~2s later. An adapter that showed one unbroken working span here would be hiding the loop, not modelling it.
(3) The goal text was WIDENED BEFORE RECORDING, per the column's TIMING prerequisite: the assessed text said "say exactly one number ... and nothing else", which is a sub-second turn the 2s watcher poll can swallow whole, erasing the very ready->working edge iter1_start/iter2_start assert. Each iteration now also writes ~200 words about the number. The counting contract that terminates the loop is untouched; the spec was not weakened.
(4) tokens_nonzero STRIPPED, model PINNED in its place - the standing hermes-column trade (1-6, 2-1, 2-10, 2-13, 3-2, 3-5). SEEN RED on this recording: `of record verify` reported "observations: FAIL - tokens: want >0 got 0" with 7/7 state phases green. Structural, not drift: `of verify` asserts against the REPLAY GOLDEN summary, produced by driving core/pkg/tailer with hermes.Parser (ModelName only), while hermes' token aggregate lives on the `sessions` row and reaches irrlicht only through ComputeMetrics, a path replay never runs. The cell's verify[] keeps the token claim at the metric tier. Unlock = extend the #766 golden lift + StageReplayStore to hermes as #775/#776 did for antigravity. cost_nonzero was already false and stays false: irrlicht prices hermes from core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go, which carries no entry for the locally configured gpt-5.6-luna.

text: Process scanner mints the transient proc-<PID> pre-session in ready — hermes' sessions row does not exist until the first user message, so this is the first thing the daemon can see
The real store session (a DIFFERENT id, source='cli') is born ready once /goal writes the first user message — the REPL boot is slow (~35 tools + ~68 skills), hence the wide budget
Spec: 'ready -> working at loop start' — /goal <condition> enqueues the goal text as a user message and drives iteration 1
Iteration 1 completes: the assistant row carries finish_reason='stop', so the turn is genuinely over and the session settles to ready while the goal judge runs
THE autonomy assertion: the session returns to working on the SAME session with no user and no driver input in between — the judge said 'continue' and hermes fed its own continuation prompt back in
Iteration 2 completes back to ready — at least two self-driven turns, satisfying the scenario's '>= 2 turns'

Spec: 'after the goal is reached: working -> ready' — the loop terminates (judge verdict done, or /goal clear) and final state is ready. The loop may run a third iteration before converging, so the only strict invariant here is that the session never enters waiting across the tail of the run; the matcher may satisfy this at iter2_done itself (delta 0), exactly as the claudecode sibling does, because the convergence turn's timing is non-deterministic
